ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is triangle SRT, with a right-angle mark at vertex S; the horizontal side SR is labeled 8, the vertical side ST is labeled 12, and the hypotenuse is RT. The problem asks to find the measure of ∠T. Reasoning: Relative to ∠T, side SR is the opposite side, and side ST is the adjacent side. Therefore use the tangent ratio: tan(T)=opposite/adjacent=8/12=2/3. Calculate T=arctan(2/3)≈33.6901°, rounded to the nearest tenth as 33.7°.

raw_record.question_text: Find the measure of $\angle T$ to the nearest tenth.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as right triangle SRT with the right angle marked at S, side SR labeled 8, and side ST labeled 12. The question asks for the measure of angle T. Relative to angle T, SR is the opposite leg and ST is the adjacent leg, so use the tangent ratio: tan(T)=opposite/adjacent=8/12. Compute T=arctan(8/12) and round to the nearest tenth, giving 33.7 degrees.
